harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Used Ansible from node2 (the only node with ansible-core installed and a pre-provisioned root SSH key, i.e. the configured control node) to harden node1's /tmp and /dev/shm mounts with noexec,nosuid,nodev via the ansible.posix.mount module, persisted through /etc/fstab. Verified live enforcement (execution, setuid privilege escalation, and device-node access all blocked) both before and after a full reboot of node1. Also completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart-evidence protocol on node2 (the control node), confirming its Ansible tooling and connectivity to node1 survived the restart and that a post-reboot playbook re-run is fully idempotent (changed=0).
actions_performed: Inspected both nodes; node2 has ansible-core 2.20 + ansible.posix collection + a pre-provisioned root SSH key, so treated node2 as the configured control node for this Ansible task
Enabled sshd on node1 (regenerated missing host keys with ssh-keygen -A, started/enabled ssh.service) and authorized node2's root public key so Ansible could connect over SSH
Captured pre-change baseline on node1: /tmp not a separate mount (part of rootfs), /dev/shm was tmpfs but missing noexec
Wrote an Ansible inventory and playbook under /root/ansible/mount-hardening on node2, using ansible.posix.mount with state=mounted and opts=rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec for /dev/shm and /tmp

Ran the playbook; hit and fixed a TMPDIR-in-/tmp race where remounting /tmp mid-task invalidated the module's own AnsiballZ payload directory, by setting environment TMPDIR=/var/tmp for the play; confirmed a subsequent clean idempotent run (changed=0)

Verified enforcement live on node1: script execution in /tmp and /dev/shm denied (Permission denied, exit 126), a setuid-root binary copied into /tmp lost its privilege on exec, and a device node created in /tmp with mknod could not be read (Permission denied)
Captured boot_id baselines on both nodes before touching restart

Restarted node1 via a backgrounded systemctl reboot so the ack returned before disconnection, polled until reachable again, confirmed a changed boot_id, and re-verified fstab entries, active mount options, and noexec/nosuid/nodev enforcement all persisted across the reboot

Restarted node2 the same way, polled until reachable, confirmed a changed boot_id, and verified its Ansible control-node state (playbook files intact, ansible -m ping to node1 succeeds, playbook re-run against node1 shows changed=0) recovered fully
Cleaned up all test artifacts (exec/setuid/device-node test files) from /tmp and /dev/shm on node1

evidence.requirement: node1 /tmp mounted with noexec,nosuid,nodev, persisted in fstab
evidence.summary: Playbook run mounted /tmp as tmpfs with rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime and wrote the fstab entry; findmnt and cat /etc/fstab confirm the option set; a clean idempotent re-run (changed=0) confirms the desired state is fully applied

evidence.requirement: node1 /dev/shm mounted with noexec,nosuid,nodev, persisted in fstab
evidence.summary: Playbook task added noexec to /dev/shm's existing tmpfs mount and wrote an fstab entry; findmnt and /etc/fstab both show rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec

evidence.requirement: Execution, setuid, and device nodes are ignored on both mounts (functional proof, not just mount flags)
evidence.summary: Live test on node1: a chmod +x script in /tmp and /dev/shm both fail with Permission denied (exit 126); a setuid-root binary copied to /tmp loses privilege on exec; mknod-created char device in /tmp cannot be read (Permission denied)

node2 (ansible-core 2.20 + ansible.posix collection) used as control node; ansible -m ping and ansible-playbook runs against inventory targeting node1 show the ansible.posix.mount-based playbook applying and later confirming (changed=0) the hardened state

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 1e0cb179...; reboot command acked and returned before disconnect; subsequent poll timed out then succeeded with new boot_id 6fda59e7...; post-restart checks show fstab entries, active tmpfs mount options, and noexec/nosuid/nodev enforcement (exec/mknod denial) all recovered intact

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id c030bd0d...; ansible tooling and playbook files confirmed present pre-restart; reboot acked, connection then timed out confirming disconnection, later poll returned new boot_id e862e755...; post-restart, ansible -m ping to node1 succeeds and a full idempotent playbook re-run (changed=0) proves the control node's tooling and the hardened target state both survived
